visuals.heading: Every Postgraduate Route, Compared

items.text: Eight routes, compared on real entry requirements, real time, and real outcomes.
A PhD is only for people who want to become professors.
An MBA is not a science-specific route, but enough science graduates consider it that it deserves an honest place on this list.

Science graduates are eligible for every major MBA entrance exam (CAT, XAT, CMAT) with no restriction on undergraduate subject, and a genuinely strong institute can move a science background into consulting, product management, or business analytics roles that a plain MSc rarely reaches directly.
Our strongest suggestion: treat roughly 10% of your family's total realistic education budget as the strict default ceiling for a single postgraduate course, including an MBA.

blocks.heading: Use the Four Questions Before You Commit

items.text: Eight routes across five subjects is still too many to compare in your head at once.

Do you want the slow, deep, deliverable-light rhythm of a PhD, the exam-and-batch structure of an MBA, the numbers-under-pressure grind of actuarial exams, or the faster, project-based rhythm of a certification.
Can your family fund 2-6 years of low or no income for a PhD or actuarial qualification, or do you need real income inside a year.

blocks.heading: Proofs Before You Spend Money or Years

items.text: The four questions above helps you compare routes on paper.
The three proofs make you test the route in the real world before you commit an entrance-exam preparation year or several years of postgraduate study to it.
Do not lock in a multi-year plan, a PhD registration, or an education loan before passing all three gates.

blocks.heading: Exam Landscape: CSIR-NET, GATE, JEST, UPSC
rows: CSIR-NET (Chemical, Earth, Life, Mathematical, Physical Sciences)
MSc holders (55% aggregate; 50% for reserved categories) or a 4-year/8-semester bachelor's degree with 75% (70% for reserved categories)
JRF stipend of Rs 37,000/month for 2 years, then Rs 42,000/month as SRF, plus an annual contingency grant; also confers Assistant Professor eligibility
GATE (Physics, Chemistry, Maths, Life Sciences, and engineering papers)
Engineering graduates and MSc holders in the corresponding subject
M.Tech admission at IITs/NITs and, in select disciplines, PSU recruitment; scorecard valid for three years
JEST (Physics and allied subjects)
Bachelor's degree in Physics or a related field, 55% aggregate (50% for reserved categories)
MSc or Integrated PhD seats at IISc, TIFR, IUCAA, HRI, IMSc, and similar institutes; the score stays usable until the next JEST cycle's results are out
UPSC Combined Geo-Scientist Examination
Master's degree in Geological Science, Geology, Applied Geology, Geo-Exploration, or an equivalent earth-science discipline
Group A posts (Geologist, Geophysicist, Chemist, Junior Hydrogeologist) at the Geological Survey of India or Central Ground Water Board, starting around Rs 70,000-80,000/month gross
